text:
Hi there,

I've attached the first page of my employment contract with the Ahornweid Cooperative in Emmen, which shows when I started.

I'm writing from my sofa, where I've spent most of the last two months. I was already off sick when the cooperative's letter arrived, so the illness came first and the notice afterwards, not the other way round.

At the beginning of May I slipped a disc lifting crates in the storeroom. My doctor signed me off completely and I'm still on sick leave now. I didn't do anything stupid, it just went. I sent every certificate straight to the office, and my colleague Henry Ellis took the first one in personally because I couldn't walk.

Then on 20 May 2026 a letter from Paul Zaugg, the manager, came in the post: the cooperative was ending my employment. Two lines, signed, that was it. I was lying flat on my back when I read it.

I've been through my contract line by line since then. There's nothing special in it about a trial period, no longer or different trial period agreed anywhere.

I earn CHF 3,080 a month and I have a family to support. Can they let me go while I'm on sick leave? What should I do now?

Thanks a lot,
Felix Reid
Mattenweg 108, Emmen

EMPLOYMENT CONTRACT - page 1

1. Start of employment
The employment begins on 13 April 2026 and is concluded for an unlimited period.

2. Position
Warehouse and delivery employee, full-time (42 hours per week).

3. Place of work
Storeroom and shop of the employer in Emmen; deliveries within the region.

4. Salary
CHF 3,080 gross per month, paid twelve times a year.

5. Working clothes
Working clothes and safety shoes are provided by the employer.

(continued on page 2)
